reading.body:
Oklahoma's mapped data center footprint consists of nine facilities, concentrated almost entirely in the Tulsa metropolitan area, with one facility in Oklahoma City and one in Durant operated by the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma.

The geographic clustering around Tulsa is the clearest pattern in this data. Seven of the nine facilities fall within Tulsa or Tulsa County, and three of those carry the TulsaConnect name, suggesting either a single operator with multiple sites or co-located infrastructure sharing a brand. The TierPoint facility is the only one with a recorded square footage, at 4,000 square feet, which is small by hyperscale standards. No power figures are available for any facility, and the total megawatt field registers zero, so the data describes locations but says nothing about capacity or load.

For AI infrastructure purposes, the absence of megawatt data is the most significant gap. Compute density is constrained by power delivery, and power delivery requires knowing what each site draws. This dataset cannot support any conclusion about Oklahoma's ability to host large-scale AI workloads. What it does establish is that the state's data center presence, as currently catalogued, is modest in number, geographically narrow, and largely undocumented in the dimensions that matter most for compute scaling.
